title: How to Use Buyer Engagement Data to Prioritize Sales Outreach
theme: Using Buyer Engagement Data to Prioritize Sales Outreach
thesis: Buyer engagement data is the key to prioritizing sales outreach and reducing pipeline anxiety. Companies that use engagement-triggered outreach see a 15% increase in sales meetings booked and a 38% improvement in lead quality. This guide shows you how to turn individual-level signals into a repeatable sales prioritization workflow.
summary: Pipeline anxiety keeps revenue leaders up at night. You know your marketing team is generating activity, but sales still wastes time on cold outreach while hot buyers slip through the cracks. The disconnect between marketing signals and sales action creates friction, missed revenue, and frustrated teams. The solution is not more data. It is better use of the buyer engagement data you already have.
key_takeaways: TL;DR: Buyer engagement data is the key to prioritizing sales outreach and reducing pipeline anxiety.
Pipeline anxiety keeps revenue leaders up at night.
Buyer engagement data is the collection of behavioral signals that show how individual prospects and buying groups interact with your content, campaigns, and sales touchpoints.
Buyer engagement data is the behavioral footprint your prospects leave as they research your solution.
Account-level intent data tells you which companies are in-market.
proof_points: Companies that use engagement-triggered outreach see a 15% increase in sales meetings booked and a 38% improvement in lead quality.

Key sources of buyer engagement data include: Website and microsite page visits with time-on-page metrics Content downloads, video views, and resource access Email opens, clicks, and reply patterns Digital sales room act
The result was a 40% faster time to first meeting and $1.2M in influenced pipeline within the quarter.
According to Folloze customer Conga, six campaigns built on two boards generated $6.3M in attributed pipeline.
